item.title: Waller Is A Proxy For The Eight Fed Voters: Berro
item.description: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager JPMorgan Asset Management, and Deborah Cunningham, executive vice president, CIO global liquidity markets, and senior portfolio manager at Federated Hermes, join Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Stocks rose and bond yields fell as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cliffwater, Blackstone Private Credit Funds Cap Redemptions
item.description: Bloomberg's Olivia Fishlow joins Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Cliffwater’s flagship private credit fund again capped redemptions at 5% in the third quarter, after investors sought to pull about 16% of shares. The biggest such BDC, the $77 billion Blackstone Private Credit Fund, disclosed Thursday that it would again cap redemptions at 5%, after its investors sought to redeem 10% of shares. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: President Will Signal Nuclear Aims Over If He Ends War, Says Former National Intelligence Official
item.description: Former Deputy Director of National Intelligence and Retired Lieutenant General Karen Gibson said that if the president declares war with Iran over it will signal he has abandoned the aims of the war, including putting curbs on the Iranian nuclear program. Gibson said that even if President Trump declares war over, it will likely not move Iran's blockade on the Strait of Hormuz unless the US is prepared to give up its economic campaign as well. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bond Market Ignored in Spending Plans: Erik Wasson
item.description: Bloomberg's Erik Wasson joins Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Real Yield." US bond yields are spiking in part because of concerns over the total US public debt blowing past $40 trillion. Not only are congressional lawmakers shrugging that off, some are indicating that more deficit spending is yet to come. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Bond Yields Rise, Waller Speaks Out | Real Yield 9/3/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: JPMorgan Asset Management Field Income Portfolio Manager Kelsey Berro, Federated Hermes Senior Portfolio Manager Deborah Cunningham, Invesco Head of North American Investment Grade Credit Matt Brill, and BNP Paribas Head of US Credit Strategy Meghan Robson. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Polymarket Launches Perpetual Oil Futures in 24/7 Trading Push
item.description: Polymarket has launched perpetual futures contracts tied to oil, stepping into a market that rival Kalshi Inc. is also seeking to enter as trading venues compete to offer round-the-clock access to the commodity.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis

item.title: Democratic Socialists Endorse Nithya Raman in Race for LA Mayor
item.description: The Democratic Socialists of America’s Los Angeles chapter endorsed City Councilmember Nithya Raman for LA mayor, casting aside some members’ earlier reservations and bringing its organizing heft to her effort to unseat Karen Bass.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Clanton and John Gittelsohn

item.title: Young Workers Move to Appalachia for Affordable Housing, Lower Costs
item.description: Tucked into a remote corner of Tennessee, Johnson City had typically counted on a trickle each year of newcomers attracted by the verdant Appalachian foothills, affordability and East Tennessee State University’s leafy, cozy campus.
item.dc:creator: Michael Sasso

item.title: Earnings Have Been "Armor" to Tolerate Yields: Bordlemay
item.description: Katherine Bordlemay, Co-Head of Equity Client Portfolio Management at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, says the magnitude and breadth of earnings strength will continue to support the market going forward. She speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger and Isabelle Lee on "Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman's Bordlemay Sees `Ping-Pong' Pattern for Stocks
item.description: Katherine Bordlemay, co-head of client portfolio management at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, expects to see a ``ping-pong of volatility'' continue in US stocks even as major indexes grind higher. She says stronger earnings have cushioned equities from rising US Treasury yields. She speaks with Dani Burger and Isabelle Lee on Bloomberg's ``Open Interest.'' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Elina Ribakova on Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: Peterson Institute for International Economics Senior Fellow Elina Ribakova discusses the war between Russia and Ukraine. She says we should stop calling it ‘hybrid warfare’ and start calling it ‘open warfare.’ (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Markets Rally as Fed Governor Waller Points to Disinflation
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Travelers Book Later and Some Trade Down: BWH CEO
item.description: BWH Hotels CEO Larry Cuculic says Americans are still traveling, but booking windows are shrinking and some consumers are moving to lower-priced hotels. He also explains how the company is helping franchisees manage rising insurance costs and the bottom line impact of the World Cup on host cities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Rise as Fed-Hike Bets Ease on Waller
item.description: Stocks rose and bond yields fell as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing. Keith Lerner, CIO at Truist, discusses current market moves, Fed expectations, and outlook for where the S&P 500 may end the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chicago Projects $882 Million Budget Gap on Bond, Pension Costs
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is projecting an $882 million budget deficit for 2027, even as his administration continues to seek ways to close this year’s shortfall, underscoring the financial pressures facing the third-largest US city.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Date Singh

item.title: S&P 500 Eyes Best Day in Month as Fedspeak Signals Rate Patience
item.description: The S&P 500 Index rose Thursday, on track for its best day in a month, as investors weighed remarks from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who offered optimism that inflation is showing some signs of slowing. Traders pared bets for interest-rate hikes in September.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: European Stocks Gain as Fed Rate-Hike Wagers Ease; Soitec Jumps
item.description: European stocks gained as traders reduced bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike following remarks from Governor Christopher Waller, while Deutsche Telekom AG advanced on news that activist investor Elliott Investment Management has built a sizeable stake.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Jaisinghani

item.title: World’s Unusually High Dollar Exposure Risks Fueling Selloff
item.description: Sift through the filings of pension funds and insurers around the world and one thing stands out: some of the biggest holders of US assets have little protection against a weaker dollar, leaving the currency at risk of steeper declines if sentiment suddenly turns.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Carson, Masaki Kondo and Anya Andrianova

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Rise as Fed-Hike Bets Ease on Waller: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks rose and bond yields fell as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 3
item.description: Oil swung as Iran claimed fresh strikes on US bases and Israel indicated it is prepared to intensify its role in the war, adding to the risks imperiling energy flows from the region.
item.dc:creator: Grant Smith, Mia Gindis and Charles Gorrivan
